Settings
Settings are global and saved locally.
Appearance
Display of the whole interface.
Theme
System follows your OS light/dark setting.
Light theme
Used in light mode.
Dark theme
Used in dark mode.
UI font
System-installed fonts only — no downloads.
Log font
Scales log/text content (rows, tables, entry detail), independent of the UI font.
Syntax highlighting
Colors for highlighted XML/JSON in the entry detail — pick a scheme or follow the app theme.
Accent color
Re-pick the theme's accent colour from its own palette.
UI scale
Scales toolbars, panels and other interface chrome, 70–160%. Also via Ctrl+ / Ctrl−.
100%
Log text size
Scales only log/text content (70–160%), independently of the UI scale.
100%
Custom themes — your own color palettes
Custom syntax schemes — your own highlight colors
Behavior
Show Context and Filtered as two separate tabs, or stacked together in one split pane.
When the filter-bar action buttons show their label: on hover, never, or always.
When each view toolbar's action buttons show their label: on hover, never, or always.
Reopen a filter on its last-used tab, or always on Filtered (new filters open Filtered).
Whether opening a file lands at the top (Start) or the bottom (End).
Only effective in the desktop build.
Desktop build only: the close button hides the window to the tray instead of quitting.
Decimal separator used when copying extraction cells or exporting CSV.
Hover-to-expand panels
Hovering the collapsed sidebar temporarily expands it; off = expand only by clicking.
Hovering the collapsed entry-detail panel temporarily expands it; off = click to expand.
Context view
How the Context view starts out: auto-expanded around the selection, collapsed, or expanded.
Whether one expansion step — a "Show more" click, and the auto-expand window around a jump — is measured in entries or in a fixed timespan.
How many hidden lines one expansion step reveals in each direction (above and below).
How much time one expansion step reveals in each direction (above and below) — the number of lines that falls within it varies with how dense the log is there.
Timeline minimap
Hide the minimap's outer covered-timespan box while the Context view is showing.
Time-based (default) positions bars by timestamp — a burst of fast activity compresses into a few pixels and idle stretches eat most of the width. Entry-based positions bars by line position in the file instead, spreading bursts out evenly; the grey background bars stop reflecting real density in this mode (every bucket covers the same fixed slice of the file's line count).
Filter tree
Show the current row at its would-be spot when you switch to a filter it doesn't match.
Also show the temporary anchor when the new filter belongs to a different file than the row.
Anchor fade duration
How long the temporary anchor stays visible before it's removed.
3s
Show the "Sources" breakdown under a merged file, listing which file each entry came from.
Text-match highlighting
Your standing preference for which text filters get their matches highlighted.
Mark matches inline in the log rows, in both the Filtered and Context views.
Mark matches in the entry-detail panel (independent of the row toggle above).
Show a filter's type as an icon or a TXT/LNK abbreviation, not both.
IDE Integration
Jump from a log entry's Location straight into a running IDE, at the right line. Desktop build on Windows only — hidden everywhere else.
The log's file path is remapped onto your local checkout starting right after this match — e.g. "Code\Projects" if that's the folder your solution lives directly in. "*" matches any run of characters, "?" any single one; use a longer pattern (more of the surrounding path) if the plain folder name occurs more than once.
Visual Studio
Connect to one of your currently running Visual Studio instances.
Pick which running instance to use.
Rider
Opens via JetBrains' jetbrains:// link — Rider itself picks the matching running instance, no connection step needed here.
The name Rider shows for the currently open project/solution — required by the jetbrains:// link.
Assistant
A chat in which a locally running LLM (LM Studio or any OpenAI-compatible server) builds filters, links and plots for you. It never reads the raw log, only summaries. Local only: just http://localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1] are accepted. Desktop build only.
Shows the chat button in the toolbar. Off by default; switching it off closes the chat (stored chats are kept).
LM Studio: Developer → Start server; the default is http://localhost:1234/v1.
Needs tool (function calling) support. "Server default" uses whatever model is loaded.
Low values (0–0.3) make tool use more reliable.
Model calls per message before the assistant stops on its own.
Not tested yet.
Log Formats
Define additional log formats and map filenames to them by pattern — the default format works with zero configuration.
Filename rules — first matching pattern wins; files matching none use the default format

Add log format
Columns
Pick a column, then select its value in an example line.
Keys
Detected in the example lines. Checked paths become columns — nested keys as a.b, array elements as a[0], keys containing a dot as ["a.b"].
Log levels
Filled from the levels found in the examples. Checked levels get a quick-filter button; anything else falls into OTHER.
Example lines
Re-suggest discards the current marks, the regex and the timestamp format and replaces them with a fresh automatic suggestion. You can undo this.
Preview
Target formats (ordered — first whose own header matches a line wins)
A file resolved to this format is split into one virtual file per target format at load time (classified line by line, first matching target wins), then automatically merged back into one chronological file. Needs at least 2 targets.
